title: The Nashville shop manager and a customer he has known for years: 'just bring it by'
purpose: People, slot 22. Dale answers as if the phone had interrupted him and warms up the moment he knows the voice. He remembers the truck and what he said about it last time, asks the right two questions, and then offers no time and takes no booking: 'whenever, I'm here.'

call.day: the Thursday of week T-7 (rule R6; people, call 33)

scenario.who_calls: A customer of the Charlotte Pike shop from long before the purchase, Harlan Pewitt, on first-name terms with Dale.
scenario.job: a popping in the front end on turns; Dale takes it for the lower ball joint he pointed out before
scenario.wants: to tell Dale it is doing it again
scenario.what_happens: Dale asks after the customer's mother, asks whether it is the same side and whether the wheel has play, says it is the ball joint and tells him to bring it by. Asked when, he says whenever, this week or next.

facts.note: No price is asked for and none is given. catalogue.json ball_joint, class truck, standard: 311.64, for the order that may follow.

prices.what: the likely job; not said on the call

script.said: Harlan! Well, how you doin', buddy? How's your mama gettin' along?
Oh, she's fair. She's still got that walker. Fussin' about it.
I bet she is. Tell her I asked about her.
I will. Listen, that old Chevy's poppin' again. Front end. When I turn.
Same side as before? Driver's side?
Yeah. Driver's side. Does it backin' out, mostly.
Mm. That's that ball joint I told you about last time. Has it got any play in the wheel? Wanderin' on you?
It will be. Just bring it by.
This week, next week. Just bring it by, we'll get it up in the air.
Alright then. I'll get it over there.
